 In it’s place we’re choosing to highlight the coding data market, which has multiple ~1 year old statups all making $~100m/year in data contracts for frontier labs:

title: datasette-charts 0.4a0
summary:
Release: datasette-charts 0.4a0 

 The new datasette-charts plugin has its own plugin hook to allow other plugins to define new chart types, but I hadn't actually used it for anything yet. I had Claude Opus 5.5 build an experimental plugins just to try out the hook and it came up with a bunch of friction points in the design. This release addresses those, which should make building additional chart plugins a whole lot more ergonomic.

 I've also added a website for the plugin, at charts.datasette.io . The new website includes a tutorial for plugin authors , and a gallery showing all of the core charts and annotations, each one linking to an interactive demo on Datasette Lite .

 Tags: datasette-charts , datasette , visualization , datasette-lite

title: Inside the AI Training Data Market — Gabe Greenberg, G2i
summary:
A frontier lab can pay more for training data it gets to keep exclusive, or take a discount on data another lab can buy too. At AI Engineer CODE, G2i founder Gabe Greenberg tells swyx how labs make that decision, how small pilot orders turn into bigger engagements, and when it makes sense to build a data operation in-house.
 We also get into what the labs are buying. A good training task should sit just ahead of what a model can do today. Gabe explains how senior engineers design the task, choose the starting data, and build a verifier that can score the result.
 Thanks to G2i for co-organizing AI Engineer CODE 2026 and sponsoring this episode. Join us April 26–27 at AI Engineer Miami 2027 .
 
 How G2i went from $15M to a projected ~$100M without VC

 From 6,000-engineer training-data projects to staff-level specialists
